uncited: - **Definition:** An optimization dividing image space into equal-sized squares of $n \times n$ pixels to reduce overhead from per-pixel visibility testing.

The family also includes safety mechanisms like [Interactive Render Quality Estimation & Cancellation](8895-interactive-render-quality-estimation-cancellation.md) to prevent infinite loops in real-time applications, and view-dependent preprocessing such as [24-Region View-Dependent Visibility Preprocessing](6608-24-region-view-dependent-visibility-preprocessing.md) and feedback loops like [Visibility Feedback with Screen Space Subdivision](3439-visibility-feedback-with-screen-space-subdivision.md) to manage out-of-core data loading.

As rendering moved to GPU-based pipelines, techniques like scalar range lookup tables were introduced to cull cells based on transfer function opacity ranges, significantly improving performance for AMR datasets [S2].

The claim states that scalar range lookup tables were introduced to cull cells based on transfer function opacity ranges to improve performance for AMR datasets. The evidence confirms: 1) The technique uses a lookup table based on scalar value ranges (min/max of cell corners) to check against transfer function opacity (Boolean values indicating if non-zero opacity exists). 2) This culling reduces load and improves performance (from <1 fps to ~3.48 fps). 3) The dataset used is explicitly identified as an AMR dataset ('meteorite' dataset with 2,377,878 cells). All facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
